projects.title: Municipal Data Migration Pipeline
projects.status: Delivered per project; reused across administrations
projects.problem: Legacy registers arrived as Excel/PDF with corrupted Bengali text and inconsistent columns, and had to land in a 95-column production table.
projects.solution: Staging tables, a rule engine encoding the SOP, composite Bengali cell extraction, foreign-key ID resolution, a transactional INSERT...SELECT with a generated account number, and reversible correction scripts.
tricky: SILENT CORRUPTION: the ACE OLEDB driver guessed column types in staging, so mixed text/number columns lost Bengali text with no error. Fix: explicit typing plus a source-vs-loaded cell-count check.
INVISIBLE MISMATCH: precomposed and decomposed Bengali characters (nukta forms) look identical but never match. Fix: NFC-normalize both sides before any compare.
SAFE FIXES: corrections written as transactional, reversible scripts on a stable join key, so any change can be traced and undone.
RULE-BASED IDs: account numbers built from a zero-padded prefix, a constant, and a running number with a length rule; one off-by-one breaks every record after it.

projects.title: Tax-Head Segregation & Arrear Engine
projects.problem: The master table stores one total tax amount per holding, but the child tax-head table needs one line per head (holding, water, lighting, conservancy and others), and every administration has different head IDs and rates.
projects.solution: A config-driven engine. Each administration's head catalog (IDs and rates) is loaded from configuration; walking the catalog in order, heads are added until their rates add up to the holding's total rate. It generates the child-table rows and the arrear-opening file, behind a Streamlit front end.
tricky: NO SHARED IDS: two administrations had completely non-overlapping head IDs, so nothing is hard-coded; the catalog is configuration.
AMBIGUOUS COMBINATIONS: a 10% total could be built from several head combinations; a simple ordered walk of the catalog replaced a combinatorial search and removed the ambiguity.
MISSING RATE SIGNAL: when a file has no total-rate column, the full catalog is applied instead of blocking; an explicit zero rate still means no tax due.

projects.title: Trade License Reconciliation & Entry Automation
projects.status: Reconciliation delivered; portal automation in progress (needs BASE_URL and a full Codegen recording)
projects.problem: Registers of roughly 200 to 1,200 licenses had duplicate license numbers, missing fees and Bengali spelling variants.
projects.solution: Three-stage pipeline (convert, scrape, UI entry) with row-level status, JSONL audit logs and a 36-column entry-ready schema. Reconciliation matched on mobile number plus business name, which found 15 genuinely missing records out of 450 rows. Fee and street normalization follow strict rules (fees never decrease).
tricky: BAD KEY: license number had duplicates, so it cannot identify a row. Matching on mobile number plus business name found 15 genuinely missing records in 450 rows.
NEVER-DECREASE RULE: when merging near-identical fees, the fee may only go up, and fee, VAT and total must all update together.
RESUMABLE RUNS: row-level status plus JSONL audit log, and a resume key that is the row serial, not the license number.
CONFIG TRAP: module-level environment reads ignore .env overrides; config must load lazily. A date constant was defined but never wired to the page call.

projects.title: Centralized Municipal Tax Platform: Phased Pourashava Onboarding
projects.problem: Every Pourashava has its own tax heads, rates, ward and street structures and legacy data formats, yet a centralized platform needs all of them to behave consistently as they are connected one phase at a time.
projects.solution: Quality focus: configuration-driven onboarding instead of per-site code, reconciled data loads for each Pourashava, and regression checks so that each new connection does not disturb those already live.

projects.title: Bijoy/SutonnyMJ to Unicode Converter
projects.problem: Legacy ANSI Bengali (SutonnyMJ/Bijoy) is unreadable by modern tools.
projects.solution: Streamlit app for DOCX, XLSX, CSV, DOC and PDF, with a patched glyph map and fixes for reph ordering and pre-base vowels. Also run as customized scripts that convert Bengali text across whole database tables.
tricky: REPH ORDER: the reph must move after the consonant cluster; pre-base vowels must move before it.
HAND-TYPED TRAP: Bengali text typed into regexes can be silently decomposed, so patterns never match; build them from code points.
PDF TABLES: dynamic schema detection and ward-column state tracking across page breaks.
